structured_output.summary: parts/room-22.mjs furnishes the Boarding east bunk room (x 55..57, y 8..11, z 10..12): three brown bunks in a row on the north wall (heads at z 10, feet at z 11), the z 12 row kept clear as the lane from the landing door, one hanging lantern over the middle bunk.
left: No barrel dresser or chest: the lane has to stay clear in a 3x3 room that three bunks already fill, and the palette has no chest or candle. A dresser would need one of the bunk cells.
The lantern at 56,11,11 hangs from the roof at y 12. The stub roof gives it nothing above yet, so `mcd check` reports it unsupported; it must be re-checked after the roof and shell merge.
The bed heads at z 10 sit against the north wall at y 8. The stub shell has no wall there, so `mcd fit` says 'bed against an opening' now; re-check after shell B merges.

The room check with the real house could not run: the shell, the landing and the roof are still stubs in this copy, so the walk verdict came only from a local test with a floor at y 7 and the door's inner cell as entrance.
Not ticked in elements.md: its 'West bunk room (4 beds) and east (3) = 7 beds' item covers the west room too, so I left it for whoever holds the west room.

waste.what: Checked walkability by writing a scratch generator that added a floor at y 7 to a copy of build.nbt and re-ran `mcd room` with the door's inner cell as the entrance, because the shared shell is still stubbed.
waste.cost: one scratch script, one rooms file, two runs
waste.tool: `mcd room --entrance x,y,z` (or a rooms flag that takes an alternate entrance) plus a `mcd fill-floor` helper that lays a room's floor from its box when the shell is not merged yet

waste.what: Worked out the three-bunk arrangement cell by cell in a 3x3 room: head and foot positions, the reachable lane, and which heads sit against a wall versus a window.
waste.cost: about four layouts tried in my head before the one that passed the walk test
waste.tool: `mcd plan` with a bed-slot option that lists legal bed placements (head against a solid wall, foot reachable) for a given box

waste.what: Lantern and bed fit checks depend on the roof and shell parts that are not merged yet, so I could only confirm them by reading the FIT output.
waste.cost: two make.sh runs and a check, with no real verification of the fit issues
waste.tool: A `mcd room --stub-ok` mode that reports fit issues caused by missing neighbour parts separately from issues in my own cells

companions.task: Confirm the single hanging lantern over the middle bunk has a roof block above it once the roof part merges, and that no bunk cell falls below light 8.
Check that the landing stair's head and foot stay clear of the bunk room's door cell and lane once the landing is merged.
